entities.summary:
Sony Group Corporation, founded in 1946 in Tokyo by Masaru Ibuka and Akio Morita as Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo (Tokyo Telecommunications Engineering Corporation), is one of the world's most diversified technology and entertainment conglomerates — creating transformative consumer products including the transistor radio (1955), the Walkman (1979), the CD (jointly with Philips), the PlayStation (1994), and the Blu-ray disc. Sony's history represents Japan's post-war technological renaissance and the convergence of hardware, software, music, film, and gaming.

Akio Morita's decision to rename the company 'Sony' (from 'sonus' meaning sound in Latin) for international markets demonstrated visionary branding. The Walkman's 1979 launch — creating personal portable music that transformed urban life — is one of the 20th century's most significant product innovations. Morita's 1986 acquisition of CBS Records and 1989 acquisition of Columbia Pictures (for $3.4 billion) established Sony as an entertainment conglomerate, not just a hardware manufacturer.

Sony's PlayStation gaming division — now Sony Interactive Entertainment — has produced PlayStation 1 through 5, generating revenues exceeding $25 billion annually and making gaming Sony's most profitable business segment. Sony Music Entertainment (including Columbia Records) and Sony Pictures (including Columbia Pictures, TriStar, and Marvel distribution) make Sony the only company with major hardware, music, film, and gaming businesses simultaneously. Sony's image sensor division supplies 40-50% of the world's camera sensors including iPhone cameras.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sony's invention of the Walkman — transforming personal music experience in 1979 — and the PlayStation's creation of modern gaming culture represent two of the most consequential product innovations in post-war consumer electronics.
